title: Gate: _from_base treats an unreadable base object as absent, so the policy read fails open
description:
Follow-up to opum-doc MINOR on opum-ai/test-skills#59 (TS-38), relayed by the leader. To fix before the test-skills release.

_from_base in skills/test-audit/scripts/tmx/gate.py returns None on ANY git failure, so absent and unreadable look the same. For the policy read in main(), None means the policy does not exist at the base and the gate prints "first adoption" and judges by the working-tree policy: with an unreadable base blob that is a fail-open, since the change then chooses its own rules. For the triage (~:556) and protected_file (~:627) reads the same None becomes empty (stricter for protected_file, an under-count for triage only if the blob is unreadable, then self_added is over-counted, so those fail closed).

Scope: an unknown ref already exits 2, so the remaining case is an unreadable object, for example a blobless or partial clone with no promisor, or a corrupt object store.

Fix shape (not built): distinguish absent (the path is not in the base tree, for example via ls-tree) from unreadable (the path is in the tree but show fails), and fail closed on unreadable with a named violation or exit 2. A test needs an unreadable-object fixture; keep within the 95-case cap or ask for a measured slot.

acceptanceCriteria.text: An unreadable base object for the policy file fails closed (named error or exit 2), not as first adoption, with a test that is red on the current code.
Absent still means first adoption, and the triage and protected_file reads distinguish absent from unreadable the same way.
No collected test case is added beyond the 95 baseline, or each added case carries a leader-approved slot request.
